title: Multi-omics profiling identifies InfC-enriched deubiquitination signatures and candidate biomarkers in osteoarthritis
abstract: This repository contains the complete R scripts used for the bioinformatics and multi-omics analysis in the manuscript "Multi-omics profiling identifies inflammatory chondrocyte-specific deubiquitination-associated signatures in osteoarthritis". The code is organized into three main directories:1. single-cell analysis: Includes scripts for data import, quality control, Harmony integration, cell type annotation (COSG), deubiquitination-related transcriptional scoring, cell abundance differential analysis, metabolic pathway analysis, cell-cell communication (CellChat), and functional enrichment.2. intersection: Scripts for identifying overlapping genes between single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses.3. bulk: Includes scripts for ComBat batch correction, limma differential expression analysis, machine learning screening (LASSO, Random Forest, XGBoost), ssGSEA, single-gene GSEA, GPSAdb-based perturbation prediction, CTD analysis, and spatial transcriptomics analysis. All scripts are written in R. The raw data used in this study are publicly available from the GEO database (GSE255460, GSE114007, GSE117999, GSE57218, GSE254844).
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: ChoRS: a 158-gene choline reprogramming score for MASLD - analysis code and derived tables (v1.0.0)
abstract: Analysis code and derived result tables for a multi-cohort, in-silico study quantifying choline-glycerophospholipid reprogramming across the metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) spectrum. Score definition. ChoRS is a frozen set of 158 unique genes in five non-overlapping modules: M1 Kennedy pathway (16 genes), M2 PEMT / one-carbon methyl donation (32), M3 Lands cycle (40), M4 ACC1-driven de novo lipogenesis (41), M5 VLDL assembly and export (29). The direction-aligned contrast is ChoRS-switch = mean(M3, M4, M5) - mean(M1, M2). Data sources (all public, NCBI GEO). Bulk cohorts: GSE135251, GSE48452, GSE63067, GSE126848, GSE130970, GSE33814, GSE89632, GSE24807. Single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas: GSE202379. Spatial transcriptomics: GSE287826. Paired 450K methylation: GSE31803. CRISPRi Perturb-seq: GSE238219. Scope. Bulk effects were combined by Fisher-z random-effects meta-analysis; single-nucleus effects were tested on patient-level pseudobulk to avoid pseudoreplication. The repository contains the analysis scripts, the gene-set definition tables and the derived result tables on which the manuscript's figures and tables are based, so that every reported value can be regenerated from public inputs. Authorship of analysis. All study design, statistical analyses, interpretations and conclusions were produced and verified by the authors. Generative AI was used only for language editing and for the documentation of analysis scripts.
affiliations: Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: An arrayed genome-wide CRISPR imaging screen of cGAS association with self-DNA identifies RNF113A as a regulator of cGAS protein abundance
abstract: RNF113A study: analysis code and reproducibility resources This deposit contains R analysis code and supporting reproducibility resources for Figure 7 and a separate supplementary Perturb-seq gene-coverage analysis from the RNF113A manuscript resubmitted to Nucleic Acids Research. The Figure 7 analyses investigate associations between RNF113A expression, cGAS–STING pathway signatures, interferon signalling, immune infiltration and overall survival using publicly available GTEx and TCGA datasets. They include: Proliferation-adjusted associations across normal tissues and within individual tissue types. Ranking of RNF113A among RNF-family genes. Pan-cancer and tumour-type-specific analyses incorporating tumour purity and proliferation covariates. Analyses of immune-cell estimates and DNA-based T-cell abundance in thoracic cancers, including models adjusted for tumour mutational burden. Kaplan–Meier and multivariable Cox analyses of overall survival, including adjustment for tumour type, tumour purity, proliferation and homologous recombination deficiency. The Figure 7 resources include the analysis script, a data-source manifest, an analysis-ready Danaher immune-cell table, frozen Ensembl–HGNC mappings and Hallmark gene-set definitions. Larger public input datasets are not included; their sources and download locations are documented in Figure7_data_sources.tsv. The script generates panel-level source-data tables, an Excel source-data workbook, validation results and run metadata. The separate script, perturbseq_coverage.R, assesses the representation of selected cGAS–STING, interferon-output and proliferation-associated gene lists in the processed K562 genome-scale Perturb-seq dataset of Replogle et al. (2022). It independently downloads the reference matrix, HGNC gene annotation and MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, matches genes by Ensembl identifier to accommodate alternative gene symbols, and generates a supplementary figure and gene-level source-data tables. This supplementary analysis assesses gene coverage in the deposited processed matrix, whose documented inclusion threshold was >0.01 UMI per cell. Absence from this matrix is not interpreted as evidence of zero expression in the underlying raw data.

title: Cross-screen transcriptomic coupling after ATP1A1 CRISPRi in K562 cells: A source-adaptive public-data validation toward a theory of cellular unity
abstract: This record contains the final results manuscript and complete reproducibilitymaterials for Paper 2 of the CELL-IU program. The study reports a prespecified public-data analysis of transcriptomicinter-program coupling following ATP1A1 CRISPR interference in two separateK562 Perturb-seq screens. ATP1A1 target engagement and energetic-programdisplacement were detected in both screens. Chromatin-regulatory displacementand specificity passed in the day-8 screen but not in the day-6 screen.Cross-screen E+C gene responses were directionally concordant. The frozen scientific verdict is PARTIAL. The results support a reproducibletranscriptomic response spanning energetic and chromatin-regulatory programs,but do not demonstrate direct Na+/K+-ATPase activity, membrane-potential orionic changes, ATP/ADP changes, chromatin accessibility, causal mediation, orcomplete membrane-energy-chromatin coupling. The accompanying package contains the source-adaptive preregistration,source metadata, canonical extracted pseudobulk tables, frozen analysis code,result records, figures, deterministic reconstruction, adversarial audit,final scientific verdict, and internal SHA-256 checksums. The underlyingsource H5AD matrices are not redistributed.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: DECONVersation Datasets Repository with Bulk Data, Ground Truth, Signature Matrices, Pseudobulk Datasets, and SIFs
abstract: This repository contains supporting data and containers for DECONVersation, a tool for deconvolving bulk RNA-seq data using embeddings derived from single-cell foundation models (scFMs). Included are bulk RNA-seq datasets with corresponding ground truth cell type proportions, signature matrices, pseudobulk datasets generated for benchmarking across varying technical and cohort conditions, and Singularity Image Files (SIFs) for the scFMs used in this work. Together, these resources support reproducibility of the deconvolution and benchmarking analyses described in the associated publication.

title: "Bio-Electric Neural Reprogramming and Cellular Voltage Potential Manipulation for Parallel Consciousness Creation: A Novel Embryonic Synthesis Framework"
abstract: 🧬 जीवन की पहली चिंगारी: क्या बायो-इलेक्ट्रिसिटी में छिपा है नई चेतना और रूप बदलने का रहस्य?लेखक: बंटी कुमावत (खोजकर्ता एवं अन्वेषक)जब हम जीवन की शुरुआत और नए शरीर के जन्म के बारे में सोचते हैं, तो हमारे दिमाग में जीन्स, क्रोमोसोम और कोशिकाओं का सामान्य विचार आता है। लेकिन क्या आपने कभी सोचा है कि एक बेजान कोशिका में अचानक प्राण या चेतना कहाँ से आती है? इस विषय पर सूक्ष्म प्राकृतिक नियमों के गहरे अध्ययन के बाद, मैं (बंटी कुमावत) आपके सामने एक नया वैज्ञानिक और दार्शनिक सिद्धांत रख रहा हूँ। मेरी यह खोज बताती है कि जीवन की शुरुआत केवल एक साधारण जैविक मिलन नहीं, बल्कि प्रकृति का एक अद्भुत "इलेक्ट्रिकल शॉक" यानी विद्युत विभव परिवर्तन है।⚡ निषेचन का रहस्य: -70mV से +10mV का जादुई सफरजब एक शुक्राणु (Sperm) का एक्रोसोम, अंडाणु (Egg) की बाहरी दीवार यानी ज़ोना पेलुसिडा (Zona Pellucida) को छूता है, तो एक बहुत ही सूक्ष्म विद्युत संपर्क (Vidyut Sampark) स्थापित होता है।इस सिद्धांत के अनुसार, इस संपर्क के होते ही अंडाणु की झिल्ली का इलेक्ट्रिकल वोल्टेज अचानक -70mV (नेगेटिव) से बदलकर +10mV (पॉजिटिव) हो जाता है। यह ठीक एक बारीक बिजली के स्विच (Voltage-Gated Calcium Channel) के ऑन होने जैसा है। यह अचानक बदला हुआ वोल्टेज एक सुरक्षा कवच की तरह काम करता है, जिससे बाकी के शुक्राणु दूर ही रुक जाते हैं। लेकिन चेतना के स्तर पर, यही वह पल है जब आयनों का आदान-प्रदान होता है और एक 'नई आत्मा' या 'जीवन चेतना' का निर्माण होता है। 🌍 महाद्वीपों के जीन्स का मिश्रण और नए शरीर का निर्माणयदि हम इस जैविक बिजली (Bio-electricity) की प्रक्रिया के साथ दुनिया के विभिन्न कोनों—जैसे अमेरिका, अफ्रीका और मंगोलिया के लोगों के विशिष्ट जीन्स को आपस में मिलाकर एक सूक्ष्म मिश्रण (DNA Mixing) तैयार करें, तो इससे बच्चों की संख्या पर तो कोई असर नहीं पड़ेगा (क्योंकि नियम 'एक शुक्राणु + एक अंडाणु = एक जीवन' का ही रहेगा), लेकिन इससे शारीरिक रूप और बनावट (Physical Features) का पूरी तरह रूपांतरण हो जाएगा।यह एक ऐसे नए अस्तित्व को जन्म देगा जिसके न्यूरॉन्स और तंत्रिका तंत्र (Nervous System) में तीनों महाद्वीपों की सर्वश्रेष्ठ जैविक प्रवृत्तियाँ शामिल होंगी। यह पुराने इंसान के हूबहू (Exact Copy) जेनेटिक ब्लूप्रिंट को लेकर एक नई शुरुआत होगी।🔬 भविष्य के व्यावहारिक अनुप्रयोग (Future Applications)मानव शरीर पर सीधे प्रयोग करने के कड़े नियम और सीमाओं को देखते हुए, बंटी कुमावत के इस 'विद्युत विभव सिद्धांत' को व्यावहारिक रूप देने के दो मुख्य रास्ते हैं:पेड़-पौधों पर प्रयोग (Plant Electro-physiology): फसलों और पेड़-पौधों की कोशिकाओं में भी इंसानों की तरह विद्युत विभव और आयन चैनल होते हैं। बिना किसी कानूनी पाबंदी के, पौधों की कोशिकाओं के वोल्टेज पैटर्न का अध्ययन करके हम फसलों के विकास की नई तकनीक खोज सकते हैं।कंप्यूटर सिमुलेशन (Virtual Cell Testing): उन्नत कंप्यूटर सॉफ्टवेयर पर कोशिकाओं का डिजिटल मॉडल बनाकर इस वोल्टेज थ्योरी और आनुवंशिक क्रियाओं को पूरी सटीकता से कंप्यूटर लैब में प्रमाणित किया जा सकता है। निष्कर्ष प्रकृति ने अपने भीतर ऊर्जा के अनंत रहस्य छुपा रखे हैं। बंटी कुमावत की यह थ्योरी विज्ञान और चेतना के उस मिलन बिंदु को दर्शाती है, जहाँ बायो-इलेक्ट्रिक ऊर्जा ही नई आत्मा का रूप ले लेती है। जब इस विद्युत विभव के माध्यम से कोशिकाएं सक्रिय होती हैं, तो वह सचमुच एक बिल्कुल नई चेतना और एक नए शारीरिक रूप का जन्म होता है। 🧬 बायो-इलेक्ट्रिक रीप्रोग्रामिंग और न्यूरल क्लोनिंग: क्या दो इंसानों में एक जैसी सोच और चेतना संभव है?लेखक: बंटी कुमावत (खोजकर्ता एवं अन्वेषक)विज्ञान और दर्शन के इतिहास में हमेशा से यह सवाल गूंजता रहा है कि क्या एक इंसान की सोच, उसकी यादें और उसके काम करने के तरीके को हूबहू किसी दूसरे शरीर में उतारा जा सकता है? क्या इस धरती पर दो ऐसे इंसान बनाए जा सकते हैं जो न केवल दिखने में एक जैसे हों, बल्कि उनका दिमाग, उनके विचार और उनका पूरा तंत्रिका तंत्र (Nervous System) भी बिल्कुल एक ही तरह से काम करे?इस शोध आलेख में, मैं (बंटी कुमावत) एक ऐसे अभूतपूर्व वैज्ञानिक दृष्टिकोण को रेखांकित कर रहा हूँ जो जीव विज्ञान (Biology), आनुवंशिकी (Genetics) और बायो-इलेक्ट्रिक वोल्टेज (Bio-electric Voltage) के अनूठे मेल से इस कल्पना को वास्तविकता में बदलने का मार्ग प्रशस्त करता है। 1. जीवन की पहली विद्युत चिंगारी: -70mV से +10mV का रहस्यइस सिद्धांत का आधार उस प्रारंभिक प्रक्रिया में है जहाँ से जीवन शुरू होता है। जब एक शुक्राणु (Sperm) का एक्रोसोम, अंडाणु (Egg) की बाहरी दीवार यानी ज़ोना पेलुसिडा (Zona Pellucida) को छूता है, तो केवल जैविक पदार्थों का आदान-प्रदान नहीं होता। ठीक उसी पल, एक बहुत ही सूक्ष्म विद्युत संपर्क (Vidyut Sampark) स्थापित होता है।इस प्रक्रिया में अंडाणु की झिल्ली का इलेक्ट्रिकल वोल्टेज अचानक -70mV (नेगेटिव) से बदलकर +10mV (पॉजिटिव) हो जाता है। यह वोल्टेज-गेटेड कैल्शियम चैनल का खुलना ठीक एक बारीक बिजली के स्विच के ऑन होने जैसा है। यह बिजली का झटका न केवल अन्य शुक्राणुओं को भीतर आने से रोकता है, बल्कि यह वह पहली 'ऊर्जा' (Energy) है जो कोशिकाओं को सक्रिय करके एक नई जीवन चेतना और आत्मा का निर्माण करती है। 2. जेनेटिक कर्तन (Gene Cutting) और तंत्रिका तंत्र (Nervous System) की हूबहू नकलयदि हमें एक इंसान की सोच और उसके सोचने की क्षमता को दूसरे शरीर में फिट करना है, तो हमें उसके न्यूरॉन्स (Neurons) और मस्तिष्क की बनावट को नियंत्रित करने वाले जीन्स को पूरी सटीकता से कॉपी करना होगा।आणविक कैंची (Molecular Scissors): आधुनिक जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग की मदद से मूल इंसान की कोशिकाओं से उन विशिष्ट न्यूरॉन-जीन्स को काटा और सहेजा जा सकता है जो उसकी बुद्धि, तार्किक क्षमता और सोचने के पैटर्न के लिए जिम्मेदार हैं।विद्युत विभव का स्थानांतरण: इन जीन्स को एक नए अंडाणु में स्थापित करने के बाद, प्रयोगशाला में कृत्रिम रूप से ठीक उसी मूल विद्युत विभव (-70mV से +10mV) को दोहराया जाता है। यह प्रारंभिक बिजली का झटका उस नए शरीर की कोशिकाओं को बिल्कुल पुराने ढर्रे पर ही सक्रिय करता है। इसके परिणामस्वरूप जो दो इंसान विकसित होंगे, उनका तंत्रिका तंत्र और आंतरिक वायरिंग (Neural Circuitry) 100% एक समान होगी। 4. भविष्य की व्यावहारिक दिशा और सीमाएंयद्यपि मानव शरीर और मस्तिष्क पर सीधे तौर पर ऐसे प्रयोग करने पर वैश्विक स्तर पर सख्त नैतिक और कानूनी प्रतिबंध हैं, लेकिन बंटी कुमावत के इस 'बायो-इलेक्ट्रिक न्यूरल सिद्धांत' को प्रमाणित करने के लिए वैज्ञानिक रूप से दो रास्ते उपलब्ध हैं:कंप्यूटर सिमुलेशन (Virtual Neural Networks): कंप्यूटर सॉफ्टवेयर (जैसे MATLAB या न्यूरॉन सिमुलेटर) पर मानव मस्तिष्क के न्यूरॉन्स और उनके वोल्टेज का एक डिजिटल मॉडल बनाकर यह सिद्ध किया जा सकता है कि कैसे समान जेनेटिक कोड और समान वोल्टेज से दो समानांतर (Parallel) सोचने वाले तंत्रिका तंत्र काम करते हैं।पादप विद्युत-जैविक अध्ययन (Plant Neurobiology): पेड़-पौधों की कोशिकाओं में भी विद्युत सिग्नलों का प्रवाह होता है। पौधों के स्तर पर आनुवंशिक गुणों और कोशिकाओं के वोल्टेज को नियंत्रित करके इस सिद्धांत के प्राथमिक व्यावहारिक प्रमाण जुटाए जा सकते हैं। 🧬 बायो-इलेक्ट्रिक न्यूरल रीप्रोग्रामिंग: दो समान सोच वाले इंसानों के निर्माण की वैज्ञानिक विधिलेखक: बंटी कुमावत (खोजकर्ता एवं अन्वेषक)क्या दो अलग-अलग शरीरों में एक जैसी सोच, एक जैसा स्वभाव और एक जैसा तंत्रिका तंत्र (Nervous System) होना संभव है? विज्ञान गल्प (Science Fiction) जैसी लगने वाली यह कल्पना असल में जीव विज्ञान और बायो-इलेक्ट्रिक ऊर्जा के कड़े नियमों पर आधारित है। इस लेख में, मैं (बंटी कुमावत) आपके सामने वह चरण-दर-चरण विधि (Step-by-Step Method) रख रहा हूँ जिसके द्वारा समान चेतना और समान मस्तिष्क क्षमता वाले दो इंसानों का निर्माण किया जा सकता है।चरण 1: न्यूरॉन जीन्स का जेनेटिक कर्तन (Genetic Cutting)इस प्रक्रिया की शुरुआत मूल इंसान के शरीर से होती है। हमारे सोचने का तरीका, बुद्धिमत्ता और तंत्रिका तंत्र की बनावट हमारे डीएनए (DNA) में कोडित होती है।सबसे पहले, मूल इंसान की कोशिकाओं से उन विशिष्ट न्यूरो-जीन्स (Neuro-genes) को आणविक कैंची (Molecular Scissors) की मदद से काटा और अलग किया जाता है जो मस्तिष्क की आंतरिक वायरिंग और सोचने के पैटर्न के लिए जिम्मेदार हैं। चरण 2: खाली अंडाणु (Donor Egg) की तैयारीएक नया जीवन शुरू करने के लिए प्रकृति की मूल व्यवस्था यानी अंडाणु (Egg Cell) की आवश्यकता होती है।एक स्वस्थ डोनर अंडाणु को लिया जाता है और उसके भीतर मौजूद मूल केंद्रक (Nucleus/DNA) को पूरी तरह से बाहर निकाल दिया जाता है। अब यह अंडाणु एक खाली जैविक घर की तरह काम करता है, जो नए निर्देशों को ग्रहण करने के लिए तैयार है।चरण 3: न्यूरो-जीन्स का प्रतिरोपण (Nucleus Insertion)अब जैविक ब्लूप्रिंट को बदलने का समय आता है।चरण 1 में काटे गए मूल इंसान के न्यूरो-जीन्स और संपूर्ण डीएनए सेट को इस खाली किए गए अंडाणु के भीतर बहुत ही सूक्ष्म सुइयों (Micromanipulators) की मदद से प्रतिरोपित (Insert) कर दिया जाता है। चरण 4: कृत्रिम विद्युत विभव (-70mV से +10mV) का अनुप्रयोगप्रकृति में जब शुक्राणु का एक्रोसोम अंडाणु को छूता है, तो एक वोल्टेज परिवर्तन होता है। इस कृत्रिम प्रक्रिया में शुक्राणु की अनुपस्थिति में उस 'जीवन की चिंगारी' को मैन्युअली जगाना पड़ता है।प्रतिरोपण के ठीक बाद, इस तैयार अंडाणु को प्रयोगशाला में एक अत्यंत सटीक कृत्रिम बिजली का झटका (Electrical Pulse) दिया जाता है।यह झटका कोशिका के वोल्टेज को -70mV (नेगेटिव) से बदलकर +10mV (पॉजिटिव) कर देता है। यह वही मूल वोल्टेज है जो प्राकृतिक निषेचन के समय एक्रोसोम के छूने से पैदा होता है। यह विद्युत विभव कोशिकाओं के वोल्टेज-गेटेड कैल्शियम चैनलों को सक्रिय कर देता है, जिससे अंडाणु जीवित हो उठता है और कोशिका विभाजन शुरू हो जाता है। चरण 5: भ्रूण का विभाजन (Embryo Splitting for Twins)दो हूबहू इंसान बनाने के लिए इस शुरुआती चरण में एक और महत्वपूर्ण कदम उठाया जाता है।जैसे ही विद्युत झटके के बाद कोशिकाएं विभाजित होकर शुरुआती भ्रूण (Blastocyst) का रूप लेती हैं, इसे प्रयोगशाला में अत्यंत सावधानी से दो बराबर भागों में विभाजित (Split) कर दिया जाता है।चूंकि दोनों भाग एक ही जेनेटिक कोड और एक ही शुरुआती वोल्टेज सिग्नलों से बने हैं, इसलिए ये दोनों भाग दो अलग-अलग समानांतर भ्रूणों के रूप में विकसित होने लगते हैं। परिणाम: एक जैसी सोच और स्वतंत्र बाहरी विकासजब ये दोनों भ्रूण पूर्ण विकसित इंसानों के रूप में जन्म लेंगे, तो उनके भीतर निम्नलिखित विशेषताएं होंगी:समान आंतरिक चेतना और तंत्रिका तंत्र: क्योंकि दोनों का तंत्रिका तंत्र और दिमागी बनावट एक ही आनुवंशिक कर्तन और एक ही वोल्टेज शॉक से शुरू हुई है, इसलिए उनकी बुनियादी सोच, तार्किक क्षमता और आंतरिक स्वभाव 100% एक जैसा होगा। वे समान परिस्थितियों में एक जैसा ही सोचेंगे।वातावरण के अनुसार नया विकास: जन्म के बाद, दोनों इंसानों को अलग-अलग वातावरण मिलेगा। वे बाहरी दुनिया से स्वतंत्र रूप से नए अनुभव (Experiences) लेंगे और नई चीजें सीखेंगे। यह बाहरी वातावरण उनकी यादों को अलग बना सकता है, लेकिन उनकी मूल दिमागी क्षमता और सोचने का अंतर्निहित तरीका हमेशा एक समान बना रहेगा। निष्कर्ष बंटी कुमावत का यह बायो-इलेक्ट्रिक और न्यूरो-जेनेटिक सिद्धांत यह स्पष्ट करता है कि जीवन केवल रासायनिक तत्वों का मिश्रण नहीं है, बल्कि विशिष्ट जैविक बिजली का खेल है। यदि इस विद्युत विभव और जेनेटिक कर्तन को सही ढंग से जोड़ दिया जाए, तो समानांतर सोच और समान तंत्रिका तंत्र वाले

title: 🤖 AI, DIGITAL TWINS & COMPUTATIONAL LONGEVITY AT THE LIMIT Artificial Intelligence, Personal Digital Twins, Causal Simulation, Single-Cell Models, Virtual Trials, and the Future of Computational Healthspan Engineering
abstract: 🤖 AI, DIGITAL TWINS & COMPUTATIONAL LONGEVITY AT THE LIMIT Artificial Intelligence, Personal Digital Twins, Causal Simulation, Single-Cell Models, Virtual Trials, and the Future of Computational Healthspan Engineering Can we test part of a 30-year longevity intervention before waiting 30 years? This flagship research volume explores what happens when longevity science becomes increasingly computational. Modern aging research produces enormous amounts of information: genomics,epigenomics,proteomics,metabolomics,medical imaging,single-cell data,spatial biology,wearables,clinical records,environmental exposures,intervention histories,and decades of longitudinal health trajectories. The challenge is no longer only how to collect more data. The deeper challenge is how to transform these signals into models that can explain, simulate, test, and eventually help guide meaningful healthspan research. The central computational vision of this book is: Human→Longitudinal Data→Digital Twin→Simulation→Intervention→Feedback This cycle represents a future research architecture in which human biological state is repeatedly measured, computationally modeled, experimentally challenged, updated with new evidence, and continuously recalibrated. The goal is not to create a perfect virtual copy of a person. It is to build increasingly useful models of biological trajectories, intervention responses, uncertainty, resilience, and risk. The book develops this vision across several major research domains: AI AGING FOUNDATION MODELS Multimodal models integrating molecular biology, imaging, clinical history, wearables, physiology, and longitudinal data. PERSONAL LONGEVITY DIGITAL TWINS Dynamic computational representations of individual health trajectories, exposures, physiological states, intervention histories, and recovery patterns. CAUSAL AI Models designed not only to predict what may happen, but to ask what could change if a specific intervention were applied. COUNTERFACTUAL AGING Research frameworks for estimating alternative biological trajectories: What might have happened without an intervention? What might happen under a different intervention? Which observed changes are causal rather than merely correlated? SINGLE-CELL AND SPATIAL INTELLIGENCE Foundation models, cellular-state maps, tissue atlases, spatial omics, and computational representations of aging at cellular and tissue scales. ORGANOID–AI LOOPS Experimental systems in which organoids, tissue chips, and computational models repeatedly inform one another. GENERATIVE LONGEVITY DISCOVERY AI-assisted target discovery, virtual screening, generative chemistry, candidate prioritization, and hypothesis generation for geroscience. VIRTUAL GEROSCIENCE TRIALS Simulation, synthetic control arms, target-trial emulation, Bayesian adaptive methods, surrogate endpoint research, and computational approaches to long-duration intervention design. WEARABLE AND CONTINUOUS PHENOTYPING Longitudinal signals from movement, sleep, cardiovascular dynamics, activity, recovery, and other continuously measurable human states. CLOSED-LOOP INTERVENTIONS Systems in which measurement, modeling, intervention, feedback, and model updating occur repeatedly rather than as isolated events. One of the central questions of the book is: Can part of a 30-year longevity intervention be tested before waiting 30 years? The answer cannot simply be “simulate everything.” Simulation does not replace biological reality. A digital twin does not automatically become evidence. A prediction is not the same as a causal effect. A synthetic control is not automatically equivalent to a randomized trial. And an AI-generated hypothesis is not a validated healthspan intervention. Instead, computational longevity must be built as an evidence-linked system. Simulation may help reduce the search space. Digital twins may help generate testable hypotheses. Causal models may help identify competing explanations. Synthetic controls may improve trial design. Single-cell models may reveal hidden state transitions. Wearables may shorten feedback loops. Organoid–AI systems may allow faster experimental iteration. But each layer must eventually reconnect to biological experiments, human outcomes, uncertainty, safety, and longitudinal validation. The book therefore treats AI as an accelerator of research rather than a substitute for evidence. A central principle is: Simulation can compress parts of the search,but it cannot erase evidence that has not yet been earned. This principle becomes especially important in longevity research because many outcomes unfold across years or decades. Models will drift. Populations will change. Measurement technologies will change. Interventions will change. Human behavior will change. A digital twin that performs well today may become poorly calibrated years later. For this reason, long-horizon computational longevity requires: continuous recalibration,model-version tracking,uncertainty estimation,external validation,population fairness,privacy protection,failure detection,and human oversight. The book also explores the possibility that future longevity research may increasingly resemble a continuously learning experimental ecosystem. Human observations inform models. Models generate hypotheses. Hypotheses guide experiments. Experiments update models. New data revise intervention strategies. And the entire system becomes more precise through repeated feedback. The objective is not computational certainty. It is structured uncertainty reduction. Designed as a large-scale Living Interactive research volume, the book contains 200 Research Gates. Each Gate represents an unresolved research space rather than a final conclusion. The Gates explore: AI aging foundation models,federated longevity datasets,generative drug discovery,personal digital twins,causal intervention models,single-cell foundation models,spatial aging maps,organoid–AI loops,tissue-chip validation,wearable phenotyping,synthetic control arms,virtual geroscience trials,target-trial emulation,Bayesian adaptive trials,mechanistic simulations,closed-loop interventions,surrogate endpoints,model drift across decades,privacy-preserving analytics,and human oversight of AI-generated longevity hypotheses. The purpose of these Research Gates is not to claim that the future can already be predicted. It is to leave structured entrances into the unknown. From data,to models; from models,to simulation; from simulation,to hypotheses; from hypotheses,to experiments; from experiments,to evidence; from evidence,back into better models. AI, DIGITAL TWINS & COMPUTATIONAL LONGEVITY AT THE LIMIT ultimately asks whether longevity science can become not only more predictive, but more adaptive, causal, testable, and continuously learning. The long-term vision is not an algorithm that decides the future of a human life. It is a computational research ecosystem capable of helping future researchers explore more possibilities before exposing real people to unnecessary uncertainty. title: Connectome-constrained models of fly motion vision predict genetic silencing no better than their wiring diagram: a preregistered test
abstract: Connectome-constrained network models are judged mainly by how well they reproduce unperturbed neural activity, yet their value as mechanistic models rests on predicting what happens when parts of the circuit are removed. We tested whether the 50 task-trained, connectome-constrained models of the Drosophila visual system of Lappalainen et al. (2024) predict published results of genetic silencing. We removed the synaptic output of the silenced cell types in each model and compared predicted changes in motion responses with outcomes extracted from the literature by two blinded AI coders, under a protocol, mapping and analysis fixed before any outcome was coded. Of 192 experiment-level results from 23 papers, the coders placed 124 in the same effect category. The model ensemble agreed with published outcomes better than chance (weighted kappa 0.49 over 120 full-text results; permutation p < 0.001) but not better than a baseline computed from synapse counts alone (kappa 0.56). The preregistered paired agreement difference favoured the wiring baseline across all modelled readouts (-0.039; 97.5% CI -0.052 to -0.021; 17 papers) and did not favour the models for T4/T5 recordings (-0.067; -0.083 to 0.000; 25 results, 4 papers). Training raised agreement from chance (untrained network kappa 0.04) but not beyond anatomy. The models most often predicted no change where silencing reduced responses. Neither a model's fit to measured direction tuning nor its task performance predicted its silencing agreement (Spearman rho 0.16 and -0.02). In five models, including the best-performing one, the lamina neuron L1 never crossed its synaptic threshold at any light level, so silencing it had no effect. Reproducing activity did not ensure reproducing the effects of intervention; perturbation benchmarks with anatomical baselines should be part of how such models are validated. Paper 11 by Thomas Ryan. Preprint; not peer reviewed. The complete PDF includes the manuscript and supplement. The accompanying package contains code, predictions, outcome coding, protocol history, audits and reproducibility records. The protocol was frozen and hashed locally before outcome coding; this is an audit record, not third-party preregistration. AI assistance is disclosed in the manuscript; Thomas Ryan is the sole author.

title: Organoid Intelligence and Organ-on-Chip Digital Twins for AI-Enabled Non-Animal Biomedical Modelling
abstract: Organoid intelligence and microphysiological organ-on-chip systems offer complementary routes for analysing human tissue functions in experimentally controlled settings. Integrating these platforms with artificial intelligence and digital-twin modelling raises distinctive challenges in biological representativeness, sensor calibration, pharmacological transport, causal identification, uncertainty estimation and translational qualification. This monograph develops a structured research agenda that links tissue engineering and microfluidics to longitudinal inference, multimodal learning, physics-guided simulation, reproducible data operations and responsible governance. Ten interconnected research themes are organised across five chapters and assessed through twenty-five distinct methodological formulations. The proposed architecture separates experimentally observable cell states from latent mechanistic parameters and explicitly recognises donor heterogeneity, batch effects, concentration loss, protocol drift and uncertainty under deployment. Each chapter combines conceptual contributions with original schematics, a decision-oriented table, a falsifiable quantitative model and operational verification requirements. Applications address drug response, toxicology, inflammation, neural organoid activity and the evaluation of non-animal methods for specified contexts of use. Research translation is framed as a staged process of analytical validity, biological relevance and prospective external corroboration rather than an automatic replacement of animal studies. The resulting synthesis supports interdisciplinary teams designing rigorous, transparent and internationally adaptable biomedical modelling systems. Keywords organoid intelligence, organ-on-chip, microphysiological systems, digital twins, non-animal methods, patient-derived organoids, biomedical modelling, microfluidics, tissue engineering, mechanistic simulation, causal inference, multimodal AI, spatial omics, drug screening, toxicity prediction, physics-informed learning, uncertainty quantification, perfusion transport, biobank provenance, model validation, FAIR data, regulatory qualification

title: Breast cancer brain metastasis: mechanisms, emerging biomarkers, and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Breast cancer brain metastasis (BCBM) is a clinically distinct form of metastatic breast cancer that causes substantial neurological morbidity and mortality. This review examines the biological bottlenecks that precede a detectable brain lesion: survival in the circulation, interaction with the cerebral endothelium, passage across the blood-brain barrier (BBB), persistence in neural tissue, and intracranial outgrowth. We emphasize how astrocytes, microglia, neurons, stromal cells, and the nutrient environment of the brain shape these events and influence treatment response. These biological features also shape disease assessment. Magnetic resonance imaging defines lesion burden but cannot reliably determine molecular status, whereas tissue sampling is invasive and plasma biomarkers may underrepresent disease confined to the central nervous system. We therefore examine the complementary roles and current limitations of tissue reassessment, blood- and cerebrospinal fluid-based liquid biopsy, molecular imaging, and artificial intelligence-assisted image analysis. Experimental evidence is interpreted according to the questions that individual models can answer. Spontaneous, intravascular, and intracranial models retain different stages of the metastatic cascade, while immunocompetent, patient-derived xenograft, and organoid systems differ in their ability to reproduce immune interactions and patient heterogeneity. Treatment is considered by subtype and clinical setting, including the need for immediate local control, intracranial disease burden, leptomeningeal involvement, previous therapy, and extracranial disease status. Clinical evidence is most developed for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive BCBM, whereas treatment of hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative disease and triple-negative breast cancer remains more dependent on local therapy and systemic indications derived from extracranial disease. Linking brain-specific mechanisms with biomarker selection, model interpretation, and subtype-guided treatment may improve the translation of experimental findings into clinically meaningful strategies.

title: Spatial, single-nucleus and pathological profiling of the invasive front in early hepatocellular carcinoma for characterizing specific leading-edge cell niche and improving recurrence modeling.
abstract: The tumor leading edge (TLE) is a critical region where tumor cells interact with the microenvironment to drive invasion and metastasis; however, its cellular architecture in early hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and computational pathology to investigate TLE in early HCC. We annotated 35 cell subpopulations and identified STMN1-high tumor cells as a key malignant subset enriched at the invasive front, interacting with Treg, plasma B, LAMP3⁺ dendritic cells and SPP1⁺ macrophages. Spatial analysis revealed three co-localized cell pairs-(SPP1⁺ macrophages co-localized with Tip-like and inflammatory endothelial cells), (LAMP3⁺ DCs co-localized with naive T cells), and (plasma B cells co-localized with cancer-associated fibroblasts)-forming a leading-edge tumor microenvironment (L-TME) niche associated with early relapse. We developed an L-TME-related machine-learning benchmark framework incorporating 71 imaging features (65 deep-learning + 6 pathological) based on the snRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics and pathomics. The pathology model achieved robust performance (mean C-index=0.77) and successfully predicted the recurrence of early HCC (log-rank p < 0.05) in TCGA (n=147) and an independent in-house cohort (n=123). This study delineates the TLE cellular ecosystem of early HCC, defines a spatially coordinated immunosuppressive L-TME niche, and provides a clinically applicable predictive tool for postoperative recurrence. Integrating multi-omics with computational pathology deepens our understanding of early HCC metastasis and offers insights into improved prognostication and therapeutic strategies.

title: Realistic coupling enables flexible macroscopic traveling waves in the mouse cortex
abstract: Traveling waves are ubiquitous in neuronal systems across different spatial scales. While microscopic and mesoscopic waves are relatively well studied, the emergence of macroscopic traveling waves remains less understood. Here, by modeling the mouse cortex using spatial transcriptomic and connectivity data, we show that realistic cortical connectivity can generate a significantly higher level of macroscopic traveling waves than artificial local and uniform connectivity across multiple oscillation frequency bands, with the strongest advantage appearing in the theta, alpha, and beta frequency bands. By probing the model in different dynamic regimes, we find that macroscopic wave activity depends on both network connectivity and excitatory coupling strength, with a non-monotonic dependence on coupling. Together, our work shows how flexible macroscopic traveling waves can emerge in the mouse cortex and offers a computational framework to further study traveling waves in the mouse brain at the single-cell level.

title: Comprehensive RNA velocity by modeling the cascade of gene regulation, transcription, and splicing from single-cell RNA sequencing data with TSvelo.
abstract: RNA velocity approaches fit gene dynamics and infer cell fate by modeling the splicing process using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. However, due to the short time scale of splicing, high noise, and large complexity of data, existing RNA velocity methods often fail to precisely capture the complex velocity dynamics for individual genes and single cells, which makes their downstream analysis less reliable and less robust. We propose TSvelo , a comprehensive RNA velo city mathematics framework that can model the cascade of gene regulation, T ranscription and S plicing using highly interpretable neural ordinary differential equations. TSvelo can precisely capture the transcription-unspliced-spliced 3D dynamics of all genes simultaneously, infer unified latent time shared by genes within a single cell, and be applied to multi-lineage datasets. Experiments on six scRNA-seq datasets, including two multi-lineage datasets, demonstrate TSvelo's superiority.

llm.summary_zh: TSvelo 是 RNA velocity 框架，使用神经常微分方程刻画转录、未剪接与剪接状态的三维动力学，并为单个细胞推断统一的潜时间。它支持多谱系数据，在六个 scRNA-seq 数据集（包括两个多谱系数据集）上相较现有方法表现更优。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为单基因与单细胞层面的动力学推断提供了更稳健的建模方式。

title: Reviewer #1 (Public review): Comprehensive RNA velocity by modeling the cascade of gene regulation, transcription, and splicing from single-cell RNA sequencing data with TSvelo
eLife Assessment: Single-cell spatial mapping reveals reproducible cell type organization and spatially dependent gene expression in gastruloids
abstract: Gastruloids are stem-cell-based models that recapitulate key aspects of mammalian gastrulation, including the formation of an anterior-posterior axis. However, we do not have detailed spatial information about gene expression and cell type organization, particularly at the level of individual gastruloids. Here, we report a spatially resolved, single-cell molecular catalog of the transcriptomes of 26 individual gastruloids. We found that cell type composition and tissue-scale spatial organization were largely consistent across gastruloids, but meso-scale patterning of specific cell types varied between samples. Posterior cell types formed distinct, organized clusters, while anterior cell types were more disorganized. To distinguish progressive differentiation from cell type differences, we developed the L-score, a parameter-free quantification of mutually exclusive gene expression. This analysis revealed spatial organization without explicit encoding, recapitulated known cell type relationships, and identified novel gene expression states and spatial subclusters within cell types. We confirmed that in gastruloids, neuromesodermal precursor differentiation occurred through a continuous, spatially coordinated process. We also showed that endothelial precursors exhibited unique spatial organization and had distinct gene expression profiles dependent on their association with anterior somitic or posterior endodermal tissues. This work enables the rigorous use of gastruloids as models for studying the molecular mechanisms underlying mammalian development and tissue organization and introduces new computational tools for analyzing spatially resolved single-cell datasets.
affiliations: University of Hong Kong
University of Pennsylvania

llm.novelty_zh: 提出参数自由的L-score量化互斥基因表达，无需显式编码即可揭示空间组织与细胞亚群。
llm.summary_zh: 研究构建了26个单独类胚体的空间解析单细胞转录组图谱，发现细胞类型组成在类胚体间基本一致，而特定细胞类型的中尺度模式存在差异。作者据此描述神经中胚层前体的连续分化过程，以及内皮前体依赖邻近组织的空间分布特征。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该工作为类胚体作为发育模型提供了单样本层面的空间参考，并附带可复用的分析工具。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及。

title: Exploring Transcriptional Regulation of Cell State via Transcription Factor Perturb-seq
abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) are primary regulators of cell identity, and understanding how their disruption affects cell state is a core objective of functional genomics. Perturb-seq, which combines gene perturbations with single-cell transcriptomic readouts, enables high-throughput measurement of the downstream responses to perturbations. This work reanalyzes two published genome-scale Perturb-seq datasets - one in KOLF2.1J human induced pluripotent stem cells, one in the K562 leukemia cell line - using a single analytical workflow. Building upon these studies, this work interprets the downstream programs each TF knockdown engages, at the level of the whole dataset, individual clusters, and single knockdowns. In both datasets, TF knockdowns reshaped cell states along lineage-associated axes. In KOLF2.1J, disruption of the pluripotency network destabilized the pluripotent cell state and revealed a bias towards a neuroectoderm lineage. In K562, TF knockdown responses highlighted distinct regulators of the erythroid and myeloid programs. Lineage specification emerged as the clearest biological signal above a generic TF knockdown program in both datasets. Cross-dataset comparison further identified regulators whose transcriptional responses depended on the cell state, providing a demonstration of context-dependent regulation across two cell lines with differing lineage potential. Together, these results characterize how TF knockdowns engage and destabilize lineage specification programs. Further, this work demonstrates that published Perturb-seq datasets yield interpretable biology beyond the original analysis when the downstream effects of perturbations are examined directly.

llm.novelty_zh: 用统一流程重新分析两套公开的全基因组 TF Perturb-seq 数据，比较不同细胞状态下的转录响应。
llm.summary_zh: 作者对 KOLF2.1J 诱导多能干细胞与 K562 两套已发表的 Perturb-seq 数据进行统一重分析，考察转录因子敲低在整体、聚类及单基因层面引起的细胞状态变化。结果显示多能性网络扰动会使多能态失稳并偏向神经外胚层，K562 中则区分了红系与髓系调控因子。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为理解转录因子如何调控谱系特化提供了实证参照，但与虚拟细胞建模关联较弱。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及定量的方法学比较或对分析结论的独立验证。

title: Position: Temporal Measurement Interval Determines Computational and Model Complexity in Single-Cell Perturbation Analysis
abstract: Single-cell perturbation analysis aims to predict how cellular states change after interventions such as drug treatments or genetic edits. A central difficulty is that pre- and post-perturbation measurements are typically observed as unpaired populations, so accurate prediction requires inferring a latent coupling and learning a transition map. In this position paper, we argue that the measurement time gap is the key experimental knob controlling both the computational tractability of coupling and the effective model complexity. We identify a critical time gap $\Delta$ that induces a phase transition, under biologically inspired conditions; for "measurement-time $< \Delta$", matching is polynomial-time tractable and the task reduces to supervised learning, whereas for "measurement-time $>\Delta$", recovering the matching is NP-hard in the worst case. The required conditions are restricted isometry of the initial states and temporal smoothness of the transition dynamics. We complement the theory with empirical evidence on synthetic and biological datasets showing a sharp regime change as the time gap increases. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a linear model can match or exceed the performance of higher-capacity neural approaches when our conditions hold.
affiliations: University of Virginia

llm.novelty_zh: 提出测量时间间隔存在相变阈值，决定未配对单细胞扰动的耦合求解是否可在多项式时间内完成。
llm.summary_zh: 该立场文章认为测量时间间隔是控制耦合计算可解性与模型复杂度的关键参数，并给出阈值 Δ 处的相变理论。在初始状态等距与转移动力学时间平滑的条件下，间隔小于 Δ 时匹配可多项式求解，大于 Δ 时最坏情况为 NP-hard。合成与生物数据显示，条件满足时线性模型可匹配或超过高容量模型。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 把实验时间设计与计算可行性联系起来，对选择单细胞扰动实验的采样间隔有指导意义。
llm.limitations_zh: 理论依赖等距与时间平滑等限制性条件，摘要未说明这些条件在真实生物数据中的满足程度。

title: Needles in the Haystack: Addressing Signal Dilution Improves scRNA-seq Perturbation Response Modeling and Evaluation
abstract: Recent benchmarks reveal that single-cell perturbation response models are often outperformed by simply predicting the dataset mean. Through large-scale in silico simulations, together with analyses of two real-world perturbation datasets, we trace this anomaly to a metric artifact: unweighted error metrics systematically reward mean predictions when perturbation effects are sparse. To address this limitation, we introduce differentially expressed gene (DEG)-aware metrics—weighted mean-squared error (WMSE) and weighted delta $R^{2}$ ($R^{2}_{w}(\Delta)$)—that sensitively measure error in niche, perturbation-specific signals. We further propose explicit negative and positive performance baselines to calibrate these metrics. Under this framework, the mean baseline sinks to null performance, while genuinely informative predictors are correctly rewarded. Finally, we show that using WMSE as a training objective reduces mode collapse and improves predictive performance across multiple model architectures.
affiliations: University of Toronto
Vector Institute

llm.novelty_zh: 诊断未加权误差指标对稀疏扰动的偏置，提出DEG加权的WMSE与加权delta R²并设置正负性能基线。
llm.summary_zh: 论文通过大规模模拟和两个真实扰动数据集发现，未加权误差指标在扰动效应稀疏时会奖励均值预测，从而解释了为何扰动模型常被简单均值基线超过。作者提出DEG加权的WMSE和加权delta R²，并设置显式的负、正性能基线；将WMSE用作训练目标还能减轻模式崩塌并改善多种模型架构的预测性能。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为单细胞扰动预测的评估与训练目标提供了更敏感的指标与基线，对基准设计有直接意义。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及

title: scDEBART: Predicting in silico Single-Cell Perturbation Responses via Large-Scale Differential Expression Learning
abstract: Single-cell foundation models trained on millions of cells can learn gene expression patterns across diverse contexts. However, for predicting genetic perturbation effects they often underperform simple regression models. We hypothesize two potential limitations: targets defined on dropout-prone absolute expression, and pretraining objectives that reconstruct static co-expression rather than encoding how genes co-regulate under expression changes. We introduce $\textbf{scDEBART}$, a perturbation-specific pretraining framework that predicts log fold-changes (logFC) conditioned on basal expression, thereby learning how gene sets co-vary across expression-change contexts at scale. To obtain reliable estimates of expression change under technical sparsity, we compute logFC from scVI-denoised expression and restrict pretraining to genes with robust detection. Pretrained on 6.28 million expression-change profiles from 66.6 million human cells and fine-tuned on five Perturb-seq datasets, scDEBART achieves mean enrichment factor (EF) of 11.96, 4-7$\times$ higher than scGPT and GEARS (mean EF 1.74-2.99), and 71.4% top-1 accuracy for reverse perturbation identification compared to near-zero accuracy for prior models. In cross-modal transfer to drug perturbations (SCIPLEX), the model shows dose-dependent improvement in directional alignment (cosine similarity 0.04$\rightarrow$0.30) with above-random DEG enrichment (EF 2.91-4.32), suggesting partial transfer of learned regulatory patterns across modalities. Overall, these results indicate that large-scale pretraining on scVI-denoised expression-change profiles provides a useful inductive bias for perturbation prediction.
affiliations: Ewha Womans University

llm.novelty_zh: 以大规模扰动表达变化（logFC）为预训练目标，并用于反向扰动识别与跨模态迁移。
llm.summary_zh: scDEBART 在来自6,660万个人类细胞的628万条表达变化谱上预训练，用 scVI 去噪后的 logFC 作为以基础表达为条件的预测目标，学习基因集在表达变化中的共变规律。微调到五个 Perturb-seq 数据集后，平均富集因子达11.96，约为 scGPT 和 GEARS 的4至7倍；在 SCIPLEX 药物扰动上也表现出部分跨模态迁移。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 提出了可扩展的扰动预训练目标，并显著提升了反向扰动识别的准确率（top-1 为71.4%）。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未说明药物扰动迁移的绝对性能，跨模态结果仅为部分迁移。

title: Tri-Scale Neural ODEs for Continuous Multi-Omics Disease Modeling
abstract: The fields of AI-based disease fingerprinting, drug discovery and repurposing are currently among the emerging frontiers of machine learning applied to medicine. One major challenge is to obtain robust $\textit{in-silico}$ modeling of disease progression while accounting for the vastly different time scales of biochemical interactions, from gene expression to protein abundance and metabolic flux. Discrete sequence models inadequately represent such multi-scale interactions, and standard Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (NODEs) often fail to train stably under stiffness (different time scales). To address this, a Tri-Scale Stiff NODE, defined by hierarchically coupled latent differential equations that model the causal relationships from genes to proteins and metabolites, is introduced and optimized in this paper in terms of reconstruction error and information-theoretic mutual information. This enables continuous-time modeling of cellular responses to identify not only the disease dynamics, but also drug perturbations that act within narrow time windows, often invisible to discrete-time approaches. Lyapunov analysis provides a theoretical guarantee that the modeled trajectories remain stable and well-behaved even under extreme stiffness. The methodology is validated using the STATegra B-cell and Traxler macrophage datasets, with the former utilized for a proof-of-concept drug repurposing pipeline.

llm.novelty_zh: 用分层耦合的潜在微分方程（三尺度刚性 NODE）刻画从基因到蛋白、代谢物的多尺度动态，并给出稳定性分析。
llm.summary_zh: 作者提出 Tri-Scale Stiff NODE，以分层耦合的潜在微分方程描述基因、蛋白与代谢物之间的因果关系，用于连续时间的细胞响应建模，能够捕捉窄时间窗内的药物扰动效应。文章给出 Lyapunov 稳定性分析，并在 STATEgra B 细胞与 Traxler 巨噬细胞两个数据集上验证，其中 B 细胞数据用于一个概念验证的药物重定位流程。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 为刻画多组学时间动态和药物扰动效应提供了连续时间建模的思路。
llm.limitations_zh: 验证仅涉及两个数据集，摘要未报告与已有方法的定量比较。

title: Spectral Flow Matching: Stabilizing Stochastic GFlowNets via Frequency-Domain Regularization
abstract: Generative Flow Networks (GFNs) offer a powerful paradigm for diverse sampling, yet they often exhibit instability and poor convergence when applied to stochastic or sparse-reward environments. To mitigate the high variance inherent in these settings, we propose a fundamental re-framing of the GFlowNet training objective within the frequency domain. We present Spectral Time-Dependent GFlowNets (ST-GFNs), a framework that leverages Fourier analysis to enforce smoothness and stability in learned policies. Our theoretical analysis proves that our proposed spectral loss is mathematically equivalent to regularized value iteration, acting as a principled low-pass filter that separates signal from noise. Furthermore, we tackle the challenge of exploration in sparse landscapes by introducing a novel autocorrelated intrinsic reward derived from the Wiener-Khinchin theorem. Through extensive experiments ranging from adversarial games and noisy sequence generation to high-dimensional single-cell perturbation modelling, we demonstrate that ST-GFNs significantly outperform existing baselines in terms of robustness, sample efficiency, and mode discovery.

llm.novelty_zh: 将频域正则化引入 GFlowNet 训练目标，并以自相关内在奖励改善稀疏奖励下的探索。
llm.summary_zh: 研究提出 ST-GFNs，在 GFlowNet 训练中加入频域谱损失，并基于 Wiener-Khinchin 定理设计内在奖励。作者在对抗博弈、含噪序列生成与高维单细胞扰动建模等实验中报告了更好的稳定性、样本效率与模式发现。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该工作为随机与稀疏奖励环境下的生成式采样提供了通用正则化思路，单细胞部分只是其跨领域应用之一。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及单细胞实验的具体设置与基线细节。
